What I found
- The compiler reported: "The method corsConfigurationSource() is undefined for the type SecurityConfig" for `SecurityConfig.java`.
- That error came from the line in `filterChain` which calls cors.configurationSource(corsConfigurationSource()). The method/cors bean was missing.

What I changed
- Added a CorsConfigurationSource bean to `SecurityConfig.java` (plus the necessary imports: CorsConfiguration and UrlBasedCorsConfigurationSource). The new bean is permissive (allow all origins via addAllowedOriginPattern("*"), allow common methods and headers, and allow credentials). This matches the intended use in the filterChain method and resolves the undefined-method compilation error.

Why this fixes it
- The call corsConfigurationSource() expects a bean/method that returns CorsConfigurationSource. Adding that method provides the symbol and a bean instance Spring will use at runtime to configure CORS for the HttpSecurity instance.

Files edited
- src/main/java/com/arpan/durga_puja_hopping/config/SecurityConfig.java
  - Added imports: org.springframework.web.cors.CorsConfiguration and UrlBasedCorsConfigurationSource
  - Added method:
    public CorsConfigurationSource corsConfigurationSource() { ... }

Verification
- I re-ran the project's error checker for the file; it returned no errors for `SecurityConfig.java`.

Notes and next steps (recommended)
- Current CORS config is permissive for development. For production, restrict allowed origins to explicit frontend domains (replace addAllowedOriginPattern("*") with addAllowedOrigin("https://yourdomain.com") or similar).
- If you prefer global CORS in another config class, you can centralize this instead of defining it here.
- If you want, I can:

  - run a full mvn -DskipTests=false verify/build to ensure no other compile issues,
  - or run the unit tests.
